Alex / Sean — quick tech notes and concrete numbers from the runtime team: 

- Batching: for embedding ingest of 5k vectors, we recommend batches of 256 vectors per request for parallelized host-side tokenization/encode. For inference->index pipelines (if you encode on your side and only call index API) we recommend bulk upsert endpoints with 1k ids per request to amortize HTTP overhead.

- Online query batching: Redwood continuous-batching is transparent for generation endpoints; for vector search we optimize top-k scoring. Typical per-query latency targets: 50–80ms median, 120–160ms p99 depending on dataset cardinality and replica count. If you need <120ms p99 at 100M vectors we should plan for dedicated capacity.

- Normalization & similarity: do L2-normalize vectors on ingest. Use cosine similarity for semantic ranking; switch to dot product only if you want raw inner-product scoring with un-normalized vectors.

- Dimensionality reduction: two approaches we can test in Sprint 2: 1) model swap to a 1024-dim embedding model (re-embed a small validation set and compute recall delta), or 2) offline PCA on your exported vectors with retraining of index. Model swap is lower operational risk.

- Migration from Pinecone: we can accept Pinecone exports (id + vector + metadata). Important: keep stable external ids. Our import tool maps Pinecone ids to Redwood ids; we recommend a dry-run: import to a dev index, run consistency checks on top-50 queries. I'll attach a short checklist in the Drive link.

- Reranker: keep reranker calls off the hot path. Our recommended flow: 1) semantic search top-100, 2) client-side lightweight filter, 3) call reranker model on top-10. This keeps cost down and latency predictable.

I'll add a short migration checklist to the Drive folder by EOD. If you want, I can include a sample node script for export/import during Sprint 1.

-Karthik
